title: Semantic segmentation detects squamous cell carcinoma metastasis in lymph node slides
summary: A DeepLab v3 model trained on 110 metastasis-positive and 132 negative esophageal lymph node slides estimated metastasis probability on H&E slides. On a separate cohort of 795 lymph nodes from 154 patients it reached 94% accuracy after noise filtering, and 96.7% in throat and 90% in lung squamous cell carcinoma lymph nodes. The authors describe it as proof of potential for assisting pathological diagnosis.
ai_technology: DeepLab v3 semantic segmentation deep neural network on H&E slides
organization: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College; Cancer Hospital of Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences

evidence.tested: Held-out cohort of 795 lymph nodes (154 patients) and cross-organ throat and lung test sets, with pathologist-confirmed labels.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; single-center origin not detailed in the abstract; cross-organ sample sizes not stated; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning segmentation localizes and scores metastatic regions on whole slides.
